Add PRLB as an underfollowed qualified-factory candidate because US ITAR/AS9100 facilities and rapid manufacturing are directly relevant to surge-capacity readiness, though defense revenue magnitude remains unverified.

Add DDD as an underfollowed AM equipment/materials candidate tied to large-format metal printing and Air Force demonstrator work; needs evidence of repeatable defense scaling beyond demonstrator contracts.

node: Civil Reserve Manufacturing Network and surge-capacity qualification layer
summary: Layer 1B expands the CRMN/surge-capacity qualification node into US-listed public equities tied to scarce qualification infrastructure rather than finished weapons demand. The strongest public-market mapping is additive/digital manufacturing capacity that can satisfy defense-adjacent requirements: ITAR/AS9100 facilities, CMMC/DoD cyber controls, secure manufacturing networks, rapid qualification workflows, and metal additive systems for hard-to-source parts. This remains a policy-to-appropriation hypothesis: candidates should stay in watchlist status until CRMN funding, program participation, direct contract awards, or disclosed defense revenue conversion is verified.
